PullRequest.Title: ci: run Agent Host E2E in its own integration test step
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes the `Windows / Electron` → `🧪 Run integration tests (Electron)` 30-minute timeouts. These were budget overruns, not hangs.

## Evidence

Both flaky timeouts from Oct 10–17 (failed, then passed when the same SHA was re-run):

| Failed job | Agent Host E2E phase | Suite running when killed | Time in that suite |
|---|---|---|---|
| [117248871338](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38983183562/job/117248871338) | 1150s (19.2 min), all suites PASS | Git Base tests | 4s, healthy startup |
| [116352693536](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/38714176482/job/116352693536) | 1094s (18.2 min), all suites PASS | GitHub Authentication tests | 9s, healthy startup |

The `spawn C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe ENOENT` and `No default agent registered` lines that appear before the timeout also show up throughout passing suites (12 times per log). They are noise, not the cause.

Step durations of **successful** `Windows / Electron` integration steps, from `pr.yml` runs Oct 10–17 (n = 317):

- **p50 23.3 min, p90 27.8, p95 28.5, max 29.8**, against a 30-minute timeout. 26 runs (8%) took over 28 minutes.
- The distribution is bimodal: **10–12 min** when Agent Host E2E is skipped (no relevant changes), and **19–30 min** when it runs. Agent Host E2E alone is therefore about 9–19 minutes on Windows.

So any slower runner pushed the combined step over 30 minutes, and the timeout landed in whichever extension suite happened to be running.

## Change

- **Separate step.** `pr-{linux,darwin,win32}-test.yml` runs the Agent Host E2E runner (`test/integration/agentHost/runner.ts`) in a new `🧪 Run Agent Host E2E tests (Electron)` step. It has the same skip condition (no relevant changes), test profile env, and arguments as before.
- **Timeouts with headroom.** The new step gets 30 min on Windows (observed ≤19 min) and 15 min on Linux and macOS (observed ≤9 min). `🧪 Run integration tests (Electron)` keeps running everything else with `VSCODE_SKIP_AGENT_HOST_E2E=1` under 20 min: Windows observed ≤12 min, and Linux and macOS keep their existing 20-minute timeout.
- **Clearer reporting.** The remaining integration step still runs when the Agent Host E2E step fails (but not after the workflow is cancelled), so one failure no longer hides the other suites' results. A failure or timeout now names its phase in the check list instead of always showing up as "integration tests".
- **Skip message.** `test-integration.sh` / `.bat` now say *why* E2E was skipped (`VSCODE_SKIP_AGENT_HOST_E2E is set`) instead of claiming no relevant files changed.
- **Tests and docs.** `build/lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts` now asserts the new contract on all three platforms: E2E step id, its fail-open skip condition, the profile on both steps, and the remaining step's condition and skip flag. The E2E README describes the split.

Local runs and DevOps (`build/azure-pipelines`) still use `test-integration.sh` / `.bat` without `VSCODE_SKIP_AGENT_HOST_E2E`, so they are unchanged.

## Validation

- `cd build && node --test lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts`: **passed** (8/8)
- `npm run eslint -- build/lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts`: **passed**
- YAML of all three workflows parses (`python3 -c "import yaml; …"`): **passed**
- **This PR's own CI** ([run 39078455553](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/39078455553)), with the `full` profile because this PR changes workflow files: **all checks passed**. The second step logs `Skipping Agent Host E2E tests because VSCODE_SKIP_AGENT_HOST_E2E is set.`

  | Job | `🧪 Run Agent Host E2E tests (Electron)` | `🧪 Run integration tests (Electron)` | Before (one step) |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Windows / Electron | 14.4 min of 30 | 11.3 min of 20 | 25.7 min of 30 |
  | Linux / Electron | 5.8 min of 15 | 7.6 min of 20 | 13.4 min of 20 |
  | macOS / Electron | 3.9 min of 15 | 6.1 min of 20 | 10.0 min of 20 |

Scenarios.Scenario: Electron integration CI when Agent Host-relevant files changed and all suites pass
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing checkout/transpile/extension compile and Electron setup complete first. The new Agent Host step then runs to completion before the remaining Electron integration step; this is the same serial ordering that previously occurred inside test-integration.sh/.bat, so the split does not add test work to the successful critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The unchanged setup-electron action may download Electron on a cold runner/cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once per platform job before either changed test step, subject to the action cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same setup action ran once before the single integration script.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before both Agent Host and remaining Electron tests.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: prepareTestRuntime may invoke npm install or npm run electron when local dependencies or Electron are missing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One check per Agent Host runner invocation; zero subprocesses on warm state, at most one dependency install and one Electron setup on corresponding cold misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same runner was invoked once from test-integration.sh/.bat and performed identical checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold setup blocks Agent Host suite launch; warm checks are local and brief.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The Agent Host runner launches suite-specific test-integration scripts, which launch filtered Node/Electron tests and write logs/temp state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Six logical suites, with at most six concurrent suite subprocesses; Linux's existing storage mode adds the filtered disk lifecycle pass after tmpfs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same runner, suite count, worker cap, and storage passes ran at the start of the single integration script.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All suite workers must settle before the remaining integration step starts.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: test-integration.sh/.bat launches the non-Agent-Host Node integration collection and sequential extension-host/Electron suites.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One script invocation and one execution of each existing selected suite; VSCODE_SKIP_AGENT_HOST_E2E=1 prevents a second Agent Host runner invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These same suites ran once after Agent Host E2E inside the original integration-script invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs after Agent Host completion and determines final Electron integration completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Six Agent Host entrypoint suites, capped by min(6, available CPU parallelism); on Linux the existing split storage mode runs a tmpfs pass and then a filtered disk-backed pass. The remaining integration collection is executed once.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workflow steps are serial on one runner. Agent Host runner concurrency remains bounded by its existing jobs value (at most six workers); each worker owns one suite subprocess at a time. Remaining node and extension-host integration suites retain their existing script sequencing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Both steps share the same allocated runner workspace, installed node_modules, compiled output, and Electron installation. prepareTestRuntime performs the same existence/version checks as before; a cold missing dependency/Electron can still trigger npm/electron setup, while warm CI state avoids it. The step boundary neither invalidates nor duplicates these caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the old script order and new workflow order both invoke the Agent Host runner once before the same remaining suites, and the new skip flag explicitly prevents duplication.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact startup and suite durations vary by platform and cache warmth, but changed and previous cardinality, concurrency, and ordering on passing runs are directly established by the workflow and runner code.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The split adds only step orchestration while preserving expensive boundary cardinality, effective concurrency, cache reuse, and serial critical-path ordering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Electron integration CI when change detection marks Agent Host E2E unaffected
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Change detection completes, the new Agent Host step is skipped, and the remaining integration script runs once with VSCODE_SKIP_AGENT_HOST_E2E=1. Before the PR, that same script ran once and skipped its embedded Agent Host invocation using the same detection result.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The remaining integration script launches Node and Electron extension integration suites.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One script invocation per platform job and one execution of the pre-existing selected suites.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The workflow invoked the same integration script once; its environment caused the Agent Host block to be skipped before running these suites.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This is the Electron integration critical path after the Agent Host step is skipped.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The ordinary Node and extension integration suite collection; Agent Host effective cardinality is zero.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No Agent Host workers are created. The remaining script retains its existing suite sequencing on each platform job.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The runner workspace and Electron setup are unchanged. No Agent Host preparation or optional downloads are reached in either version when detection is definitively false.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the workflow conditions and constant skip environment establish the same effective work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Suite duration varies, but there is no uncertain changed multiplicity: Agent Host remains zero and the remainder remains one invocation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; unaffected changes retain the prior skip behavior and expensive-work cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Electron integration CI when Agent Host E2E fails
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Agent Host runner completes its existing bounded fan-out and reports failure. The new status-aware condition then deliberately runs the full remaining integration script, so final job completion waits for those suites; previously test-integration.sh/.bat exited after the failed runner and did not reach them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: After an Agent Host failure, launch the remaining Node integration and extension-host/Electron test processes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One additional integration-script invocation on this failure path, reaching each remaining selected suite once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The enclosing integration script stopped immediately after the Agent Host runner returned nonzero, so these later suites were not executed in that job.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly extends failing-job completion until the independent suites finish, bounded by the existing 20-minute step timeout.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One failed Agent Host run plus the complete remaining Node and extension-host integration collection. The extra work scales with the number and duration of those remaining suites, not with Agent Host item count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Agent Host workers remain capped at six and finish first. The newly reached remaining integration script is serial with that phase rather than concurrent, so there is no aggregate process burst across the two phases.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The remainder reuses the same workspace and Electron installation. It does not rerun Agent Host because the skip flag is fixed to 1; no new cache or unbounded retained state is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed condition explicitly admits the integration step when agent-host-e2e.outcome is failure, and the old scripts exited before subsequent suites on a nonzero runner result.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure frequency and exact added minutes are workload-dependent; the upper bound is the explicit 20-minute timeout. The extra boundary work itself is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. This bounded failing-path latency and runner consumption is the explicit product behavior of collecting independent suite results after an Agent Host failure, not accidental duplicate work; removing it would defeat the stated reporting semantics, and successful-run throughput is unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all seven changed files and traced the changed CI paths through test selection, runner preparation, subprocess fan-out, cache behavior, and failure scheduling. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found; the only added expensive work occurs intentionally after Agent Host failures to collect the remaining suite results and is bounded by the existing timeout.
